Source. Steps 11–15 of the supplied proof of the selected node graph_chart; the facts produced there by steps 3, 7 and 9 (ξ_N(x)(α) = α(ιe), u(0) = 0, Du(0) = 0, Γ(B) ⊆ N, u C¹ on B) are hypotheses here. Orientations: Simon Ch. 6, 2.2. Uses the accepted declarations Submission.dgcr_graph_orientation_jacobian (key graph_orientation_jacobian), Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg (key orientation_sign) and Submission.dsmc_chart_range_subset_tangentSpace (key chart_range_tangent).
Notation. B := ball(0, δ) ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}; Γ(v) := x + ιv + ι'u(v); Σ := Γ(B); e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1; for a linear L : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P, α(Le) := α(Le_0, …, Le_n); J(v) := √det(DΓ(v)*∘DΓ(v)).
1. (The Jacobian orientation of the graph; parent step 12.) Apply Submission.dgcr_graph_orientation_jacobian with n + 1 in place of n (0 < n + 1), k, ι, ι', u, z := x and s := δ (orthogonality, δ > 0, u C¹ on B): there are ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and β : ℝ^P → Λ^{n+1}(ℝ^P), both continuous on Σ, such that (a) ξ(y)(β(y)) = 1 for every y ∈ Σ; (b) for every v ∈ B, ξ(Γ(v)) is a unit orientation of the subspace range DΓ(v); (c) α(DΓ(v)e) = J(v)·ξ(Γ(v))(α) for every v ∈ B and every α.
2. (Γ is C¹ on B and maps B into N.) Γ is C¹ on B, as the sum of a constant, the linear isometry ι and ι' ∘ u (ContDiffOn.add, LinearIsometry.contDiff, ContDiff.comp_contDiffOn); in particular Γ is continuous on B. By hypothesis Γ(B) ⊆ N.
3. (Dimension of an oriented plane.) If ζ is a unit (n+1)-orientation of a subspace Q, the witnessing orthonormal family τ : Fin (n+1) → ℝ^P is linearly independent and spans Q, so finrank Q = n + 1 (finrank_span_eq_card, Fintype.card_fin).
4. (Tangent planes along the graph and the pointwise sign; parent steps 11–12.) Fix v ∈ B. IsOrientation at Γ(v) ∈ N gives a subspace Q_v with (Q_v : Set) = tangentSpace N (Γ(v)) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_N(Γ(v))) Q_v. By Submission.dsmc_chart_range_subset_tangentSpace (P, r := 1, d := n + 1, the open set B, ψ := Γ, which is C¹ on B with Γ(B) ⊆ N), every DΓ(v)h lies in tangentSpace N (Γ(v)) = Q_v; hence range DΓ(v) ≤ Q_v. By step 3 applied to 1(b) and to ξ_N(Γ(v)), both subspaces have finrank n + 1, so range DΓ(v) = Q_v (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq). Thus ξ(Γ(v)) and ξ_N(Γ(v)) are unit orientations of the same subspace Q_v, and Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg gives ξ_N(Γ(v)) = ξ(Γ(v)) or ξ_N(Γ(v)) = −ξ(Γ(v)).
5. (The sign function.) For v ∈ B let s(v) := ξ_N(Γ(v))(β(Γ(v))). Since Γ(v) ∈ Σ, 1(a) gives ξ(Γ(v))(β(Γ(v))) = 1; so s(v) = 1 in the first case of step 4 and s(v) = −ξ(Γ(v))(β(Γ(v))) = −1 in the second. Hence s(v) ∈ {1, −1} for every v ∈ B.
6. (s is continuous on B; parent step 13.) v ↦ ξ_N(Γ(v)) is continuous on B, since ξ_N is continuous on N (IsOrientation), Γ is continuous on B and maps B into N (ContinuousOn.comp). v ↦ β(Γ(v)) is continuous on B, since β is continuous on Σ and Γ maps B into Σ. Evaluation of a continuous linear functional at a covector is jointly continuous, so s is continuous on B (ContinuousOn.clm_apply).
7. (s(0) = 1; parent step 14.) Γ(0) = x + ι0 + ι'u(0) = x because u(0) = 0. u is differentiable at 0 (C¹ on the open set B ∋ 0), so by the chain rule DΓ(0) = ι + ι' ∘ Du(0) = ι, since Du(0) = 0. For a linear isometry, ι* ∘ ι = id (LinearIsometry.adjoint_comp_self), so det(DΓ(0)*∘DΓ(0)) = det(id) = 1 and J(0) = √1 = 1. Thus 1(c) at v = 0 reads α(ιe) = ξ(x)(α) for every α; together with the hypothesis ξ_N(x)(α) = α(ιe) this gives ξ_N(x) = ξ(x) (equality of continuous linear functionals, checked on every α). Hence s(0) = ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 by 1(a), as x = Γ(0) ∈ Σ.
8. (s ≡ 1 on B; parent step 13.) B is convex, hence preconnected (Convex.isPreconnected). Suppose s(v) = −1 for some v ∈ B. Since s is continuous on the preconnected set B and 0 lies between s(v) = −1 and s(0) = 1, the intermediate value theorem (IsPreconnected.intermediate_value) gives w ∈ B with s(w) = 0, contradicting s(w) ∈ {1, −1} (step 5). Hence s(v) = 1 for every v ∈ B.
9. (Conclusion; parent step 15.) Let v ∈ B. The second case ξ_N(Γ(v)) = −ξ(Γ(v)) of step 4 would give s(v) = −1, contradicting step 8; hence ξ_N(Γ(v)) = ξ(Γ(v)). Substituting this into 1(c) gives α(DΓ(v)e_0, …, DΓ(v)e_n) = √det(DΓ(v)*∘DΓ(v)) · ξ_N(Γ(v))(α) for every (n+1)-covector α. ∎

range DΓ(v) ⊆ T_{Γv}N = Q_v (dsmc_chart_range_subset_tangentSpace) and both have dimension n + 1, so ξ_N(Γv) = ±ξ(Γv) (orientation_sign).
s(v) := ξ_N(Γv)(β(Γv)) ∈ {1, −1} is continuous on the preconnected ball B.
DΓ(0) = ι and J(0) = 1, so ξ(x) = ξ_N(x) and s(0) = 1; by the intermediate value theorem s ≡ 1, so ξ_N∘Γ = ξ∘Γ on B, which gives the formula.
